# Panel J3, round 3: the busy recruiter

Persona: a recruiter or engineer seeing the site for the first time, quick to lose interest. Judged only from the 1440 and 1024 panel sheets, the two `clips-panel.json` maps and the static 1024 scene sheets. The visitor scrolled at ~250 px/s and stopped 2 s at each heading. Per-screen detail is in `panel-j3.json` (103 screen rows).

## Verdict in one paragraph

Gorgeous, distinctive and much better paced in the middle than at the ends. I would have kept scrolling on **69% of screens at 1440 (34/49)** and **63% at 1024 (34/54)**. I would not have waited for the first real information: the name lands at ~0:09 and the About text at ~0:34 (~0:30 at 1024). The things I came for (flagship projects, the kill-list, contact) are the smallest, densest and emptiest screens, while mood plates get the big pictures. The page runs ~4 minutes; about 40% of that is hiring evidence. Contact comes at ~4:00 and carries "Resume, coming soon".

Scores (0-10): keepScrolling **6**, tempo **6**, discovery **5.5**.

## 1. Would I keep scrolling? Yes rate by part

| Part (as I see it) | 1440 screens | 1440 yes | 1024 screens | 1024 yes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening and hero (Hogwarts flight, sea, name) | 1 | 1/1 | 1 | 1/1 |
| Act I card and contents (ghost ship, "A research journal in four acts") | 2-3 | 2/2 | 2-3 | 2/2 |
| About ("A builder of quantitative systems") | 4 | 1/1 | 4-5 | 1/2 |
| Journey ("How the methodology was earned") | 5-8 | 4/4 | 6-9 | 3/4 |
| Act II card, work intro, gauntlet (3 Idiots chalkboard) | 9-12 | 3/4 | 10-13 | 3/4 |
| Projects (flagship research, pipeline, "See the thesis") | 13-19 | 6/7 | 14-21 | 6/8 |
| Systems ("What I can actually do") | 20-21 | 1/2 | 22-24 | 2/3 |
| Kill-list | 22-24 | 1/3 | 25-27 | 1/3 |
| Intermission and film plates ("Three films and a game") | 25-30 | 5/6 | 28-32 | 4/5 |
| Act III card and Beyond (golden hour, three arenas, satchel, WANTED) | 31-36 | 4/6 | 33-40 | 4/8 |
| Writing (cream journal) | 37-39 | 1/3 | 41-43 | 1/3 |
| Voices ("In their words") | 40-41 | 1/2 | 44-45 | 1/2 |
| Act IV card and Principles (Great Hall, Marauder's Map) | 42-45 | 3/4 | 46-50 | 3/5 |
| Contact and credits | 46-49 | 1/4 | 51-54 | 2/4 |
| **Total** | 49 | **34 (69.4%)** | 54 | **34 (63.0%)** |

What pulls me on (yes): the Journey (a new picture and a story beat every 2-4 s, an honest "they failed out-of-sample" hook), the chalkboard reveals ("Treat every backtest as guilty until proven innocent"), the numbers (3 survivors, +1.19, 470; 3,000+ / 25% / 10-15), the self-drawing chart with a toggle, the film plates (a new picture every ~3 s), the golden-hour sunrise, the WANTED poster, the paper-to-pine-skyline dissolve, the Great Hall and the parchment rise.

What loses me (no): the 20 s before any information, the About text wall (second block at 1024), in-between transition frames with no heading (1440 screen 10, 1024 screens 9/11/33), near-empty dark screens (1440 screen 21), the kill-list as a table of rows, repeats (Black Pearl, the pen photo, "What is a machine?"), the sunset held 6-8 s for two lines, dense personal side columns, "soon" placeholders in Writing, the repeated principles card, credits fine print.

Screens at 1440 that are "no": 10, 15, 21, 23, 24, 26, 32, 34, 37, 38, 41, 45, 47, 48, 49. At 1024: 5, 9, 11, 17, 20, 24, 26, 27, 29, 33, 35, 37, 38, 41, 42, 45, 49, 50, 53, 54. The last three or four screens are a natural end of page, so those "no" answers cost little.

## 2. Tempo

| Act | Tempo | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| Opening and hero | slow | Ceremonial and gorgeous, but ~9 s to the name plus ~8 s of static hero: ~20 s before any information. |
| Act I card and contents | slow | Porthole reveal is brisk for a second, then ~8 s on one ship picture with a one-line caption. |
| About | slow | The least cinematic part: a text block held 6-8 s; a second text wall at 1024. |
| Journey | medium | Best rhythm on the page: a step and a new picture every 2-4 s, with stakes. |
| Act II card, work intro, gauntlet | medium | Chalkboard reveal is brisk; then up to 6 s of text-only hold. |
| Projects | slow | Dense small text and big empty dark; the chart screens liven it up. The part I came for is the heaviest. |
| Systems | medium | Drone photo and heading are lively; the map under it is sparse. |
| Kill-list | slow | Strong hook, then a table of rows that repeats. |
| Intermission and film plates | brisk | A new picture every ~3 s: the most watchable run, though it recaps films already shown twice. |
| Act III card and Beyond | medium | Sunrise grade is cinematic; then 6-8 s on one image and dense side columns; the poster is quick. |
| Writing | slow | Palette flip is great, but "soon" pages feel empty for 5-6 s. The skyline dissolve is brisk. |
| Voices | medium | Readable proof, then a transitional wipe. |
| Act IV card and Principles | slow | Great Hall is stunning; the parchment then repeats one card for 12-14 s with 4 s static holds. |
| Contact and credits | slow | Contact lands well; credits fade to fine print and black. Natural end. |

Overall rhythm: a long slow start, a good run through Journey and the first chalkboards, a heavy middle of text-dense projects, a brisk film recap, then a slow, atmospheric back half. Stops (the 2 s at headings) often land on identical frames (1440 clips 37-39 are six seconds of the same text screen), so nothing living moves while I pause.

## 3. Game discovery

What invited me to play, first screen noticed, and whether I would try it (both widths unless noted):

| Thing | First screen | Would I try? |
|---|---|---|
| "Play" on the opening (the film starts by itself, so it is unclear what Play does) | 1 | yes |
| "Skip to the research / Skip intro" micro-links, top right | 1 | yes, if I noticed them (tiny) |
| Hero buttons "View the quant portfolio" and "Director's cut (sound on)" | 1 | portfolio yes; Director's cut no (sound on at a desk) |
| "Egg hunt 0/12" pill in the nav (stays 0/12 all run) | 1 | maybe, only if bored |
| Teal bracket on the horizon and the compass medallion in the hero (look like targets) | 1 | yes |
| "Jack's compass" and the route mini-map with "parley?" and a skull marker | 4 (1440) / 4 (1024) | yes: it advances as I scroll |
| Contents list "A research journal in four acts" (the egg-hunt sentence is in tiny body copy) | 3 | list yes; I would not read the paragraph |
| Small drone glyph drifting across the pen photo | 10 (1440) / 11 (1024) | yes: moving and unexplained |
| Chart scenario toggle and self-drawing equity curve | 18 (1440) / 21 (1024) | yes: clearest affordance on the page |
| "Take off" chip on the homemade drone photo | 20 (1440) / 22 (1024) | yes, if I notice it (very small, no pulse) |
| "Dead Eye" pill beside the kill-list heading | 22 (1440) / 25 (1024) | yes: a hook, but unexplained |
| "Three films and a game": four act buttons, "Still hunting? Your egg count is at the top right" | 25 (1440) / 28 (1024) | buttons yes; egg nudge maybe |
| Satchel inventory icons with check marks | 35 (1440) / 39 (1024) | maybe, one hover |
| WANTED poster with a reply-by-email line | 36 (1440) / 39-40 (1024) | yes |
| Tiny galloping horse on the cream journal page | 38 (1440) / 42 (1024) | yes: looks like an egg |
| Candle "A S" bracket and "Lumos" line on contact | 46 (1440) / 51-52 (1024) | yes, but I only meet it at ~4:00 |
| Sound and motion icons beside the Egg hunt pill; Menu | 1 | Menu yes; sound no |

The invitations are real and varied, but nearly all are tiny. The only sentence that says there is a game (S3) is a few lines of small body copy, the counter never moves, and nothing pulses. A recruiter would likely try the chart toggle and maybe the drone, and not know the rest exists.

## 4. Findings (broken-looking or off-putting)

High
- **First ~20 s carry no information** (1440 clips 1-10, 1024 clips 1-10). Name arrives in clip 5 (~0:09), then a static hero; About at ~0:34 / ~0:30.
- **The hiring-relevant core is the least legible** (1440 screens 13 and 17, clips 42-53; 1024 screens 14-20, clips 39-52): small grey body and mono text, large empty dark areas (1440 clip 43: lower-left half blank), bullet walls.
- **Contact is late and carries a placeholder** (1440 clips 121-122, 1024 clips 116-117, static scene A40): "Resume, coming soon" under the email button, reached at ~4:00 / ~3:50.

Medium
- "Play" stays visible while the flight is already running (clips 1-2); skip links are tiny.
- Hero identity line ("Self-taught high-school quant, Landon School, class of 2027") and both buttons are tiny mono (clips 7-10).
- Dead or near-empty frames: 1440 clips 62-63 (near-black with a blue board and faint text), the Kraken's Storm sea (1440 clip 30, 1024 clips 28-29).
- Stops land on in-between frames: 1440 clips 34-35 and 1024 clips 32-33 (dim pen photo, a tiny drone glyph, no heading); "The Workshop" title flashes as the picture leaves.
- Static dwells of 4-6 s with identical frames (1440 clips 37-39, 64-66, 71-72; 1024 clips 35-36, 108-109).
- Writing is "soon" with draft titles (1440 clips 97-101, 1024 clips 92-96).
- Repetition: Black Pearl three times, the pen photo twice, the four films three times; "What is a machine?" interrupts the projects.
- Principles: one parchment card repeated 4-5 times (1440 clips 114-119, 1024 clips 107-113).
- The game hint is tiny text; the egg counter never changes (clips 16-17 at 1440, 15 at 1024).
- Length: ~4:16 at 1440, ~4:04 at 1024; ~40% hiring evidence.

Low
- "The Crossing" flashes for under a second over the ship (1440 clip 15, 1024 clip 14) and reads as a flicker.
- Noisy barcode-like strip at the top of the cream-to-night dissolve (1440 clip 104, 1024 clip 98).
- Unexplained bracket glyph hopping between kill-list rows (1440 clips 67-69, 1024 clips 63-66); at 1440 clip 68 it sits on the edge of row text.
- Compass medallion seems to sit over the About traits columns (1024 clip 21).
- Credits and fan-tribute text are ~9-10 px grey on black (1440 clips 126-127, 1024 clips 119-121).

## What I would change first (for a recruiter)

1. Name and role in the first 3 seconds, or a visible skip that does not need reading; hold the hero for less.
2. Give the project screens the plate treatment: bigger type, one metric per screen, fewer bullets, no blank half-screens.
3. Put a real résumé link (or drop "coming soon") and a Contact item where a recruiter will find it before minute 4.
4. Trim repeats (Black Pearl, pen photo, film recap, principles cards) and fill or remove the "soon" Writing pages.
5. Make one game invitation obvious: a pulsing "Take off" and a counter nudge when the first egg is nearby.
